arguments.summary: A credential compromise originating from external IP 91.219.236.174 led to unauthorized access via the account j.martinez. The attacker conducted reconnaissance using an Nmap-like scan against an internal IT asset. UEBA analysis showed low anomaly scores, indicating stealthy behavior. The incident was contained without evidence of lateral movement or data exfiltration.

arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was detected and mitigated. The adversary gained initial access via a compromised endpoint (WS-FIN-042) and exfiltrated Kerberos TGT data. A golden ticket was used to authenticate from IP 10.0.12.10, targeting Engineering and DevOps OUs. The source C2 IP 198.51.100.23 was blocked, the 'svc_kerberos' service account was revoked, the 'krbtgt' account was reset twice, and domain controllers were hardened via Ansible. A keylogger was detected on the pivot host.

C2 beacon established from WS-FIN-042 to 198.51.100.23 (Cobalt Strike).
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating credential dumping attempt.
Lateral movement: SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50.
Golden Ticket usage detected: Authentication from 10.0.12.10 (source) to Engineering/DevOps resources using forged TGT.
Incident response initiated: 'svc_kerberos' account revoked and 'krbtgt' account reset.
C2 IP 198.51.100.23 blocked at firewall (outbound).
Full EPP scan on 10.0.12.10 detected 'Keylogger.Linux.Snake.D' at /usr/sbin/.klogd.
Ansible playbook 'windows_domain_hardening.yml' executed on DC-PRIMARY and DC-SECONDARY to enforce security policies.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was detected originating from a malicious actor using IP 203.0.113.88. The initial access vector was a phishing email that executed an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to the deployment of a malicious DLL via rundll32.exe. The attacker established C2 communication and modified the host file. Compromised service accounts were used to propagate across 200 production servers. Containment actions included revoking four critical service accounts and rotating all local credentials across the production environment.

Encoded PowerShell command executed from Outlook process (T1566.001).
Malicious DLL loaded via rundll32.exe from Temp directory (T1218.011).
Outbound C2 beacon established to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Incident response initiated after detection of lateral movement across prod-servers.
Four critical service accounts (svc-backup, svc-sql-prod, admin-deploy, svc-monitoring) revoked via IAM/PAM.
Ansible playbook 'emergency_credential_rotate.yml' executed across 200 production hosts to rotate local credentials and revoke SSH keys.
